subject.title: fix(gateway): bound BOOT.md file read size

question: Should the BOOT.md size-cap fix preserve current symlink-following behavior, or should BOOT.md become regular-file-only as intentional hardening?
rationale: The memory bound is clearly useful, but the chosen helper also changes an existing filesystem compatibility boundary that automation should not decide silently.

options.title: Preserve symlink compatibility
options.body: Keep this PR focused on bounding memory use while retaining current symlink-following BOOT.md behavior.

options.title: Accept regular-file-only BOOT.md
options.body: Treat symlink rejection as intentional hardening, then require explicit tests, proof, and release-note context for the behavior change.

recommendation.title: Preserve symlink compatibility
recommendation.body: Keep this PR focused on bounding memory use while retaining current symlink-following BOOT.md behavior.
